steps.what: Count pieces for this canceling run
Feed mail into postage canceling devices
Hand stamp mail to cancel postage

tasks.design: A piece count for the run is the number of items already accepted in {OPS_SYSTEM}. The clerk feeds mail into the postage canceling devices or hand stamps mail to cancel postage. The count does not feed the device.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk counted the stack before feeding it.
tasks.enabler_now: Accepted items already have a count.
tasks.still_hard: Feeding the device and hand stamping stay with the clerk.
tasks.altitude: The canceling work does not change. Only the prior count of the stack is removed.

evidence.claim: A count of stored accepted items is arithmetic. Feeding a canceling device and hand stamping stay with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a stack is ready to cancel and ends when the stack has been fed or hand stamped.
An accepted item has item id and run id. The count is how many rows share the run. It is not a judgement of postage.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the stack does not match the stored count.
research_questions: Which runs matched the count, and which the clerk set aside?

already_counted.description: The counter or review time is already in the clerk's step.

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the stack does not match the count. High: the count is stored and the clerk still feeds or stamps. The range stays under the net.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Open the money orders waiting to be cashed
Match the order amount to the stored issue
Decide the money order can be cashed

tasks.design: Money orders waiting to be cashed are opened from {BANK}. The amount on the presented order is compared with the stored issue. A mismatch stays unmatched. The clerk decides, then cashes the order. The screen does not pay out.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk looked up the issue in a book and counted the payout.
tasks.enabler_now: The issue amount is stored against the order id.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding a mismatch, checking the person, and handing over the cash stay with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk holds the cash and sees the order.

ambition.what: A matching order can be decided in the same visit, and the clerk still cashes it.

tasks.altitude: The clerk decides before any cash moves.

evidence.claim: Comparing a presented amount with a stored issue is a field check. Paying out stays with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

The source pack says tools that log who did what, and schedules based on behaviour, need consent where a works council has that right. This work does not score clerks. Paying out, filing a theft report, or sending a referral is signed by the clerk. Other countries differ.

assumptions: The work starts when a money order is presented and ends when the clerk has paid it or refused it.
An issue row has order id, amount, and status, written when the order was sold. A presented order with no row is not a match.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.
A missing weight, amount, or form field is not invented. The clerk does that part.
The incremental hour updates the opened record when its source row changes.
unknowns: How often the presented order is not in the book.
research_questions: Which orders matched and were cashed, and which the clerk refused?

incremental.description: Update the opened record when its source row changes.

approvals.approved_version: The money order id and amount that match the stored issue

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Low: the order is not in the book. High: the id and amount match and the clerk still decides and pays. The range stays under the net.

steps.what: Open retail items and other office supplies
Order the items the counter is short of

tasks.design: Retail items and other supplies for office use are listed in {PROCUREMENT} with the quantity on hand. The clerk orders what the counter is short of. The list does not place the order.
tasks.previous_blocker: The clerk walked the shelves and wrote an order on paper.
tasks.enabler_now: The quantity on hand is stored.
tasks.still_hard: Deciding what is short, and what to order, stays with the clerk.
tasks.human_edge: The clerk knows what the counter is about to run out of.

ambition.what: The stock list is ready when the clerk orders, and the clerk still chooses the lines.

tasks.altitude: The clerk selects every line before the order is sent.

evidence.claim: A stock list can show quantity on hand. Choosing what to order stays with the clerk. A stored rate or form can be filled when weight, destination, service, and amount are already fields. The clerk still handles the item, the cash, and the signature. A payout or a filing stops when a stored id does not match.

assumptions: The work starts when the counter needs supplies and ends when the clerk has sent the order or decided not to.
A stock row has item id and quantity on hand, updated by receipts. The order contains only lines the clerk selected.
Time a system already spends running is not counted as the clerk's effort.

unknowns: How often the quantity on hand is wrong.
research_questions: Which orders the clerk sent, and which shortages were left?

reach: The cash owner can see which money order the clerk cashed.
